why: The 25.0% stomach-upset claim takes the urgent-care share as a share of all animals (wrong base), the 6.0% skin claim rounds 32% to a third too early (18% ÷ 3), and the surgery-referral claim is the one statement about data not covered that sourceHas lists.
Threshold question on a tight 4kg grid: 23kg leaves out the set-up times, 27kg spreads the machine cost over 365 days, and 35kg leaves out the hand set-up time; no slip lands on 31kg.

6 points reads the 'considered buying' row (46.3% against 40.5%), 2 points reads either usage row (30.6% against 28.7%, or 16.2% against 14.1%), and 31 points gives the gap as a percentage of the one-person rate (21.8 ÷ 71.2) instead of in points.

The health ministry and research council claims come true on the wrong base (non-industry income, $131m: 7.6% and 44%), and 57% public funding is a near miss that leaves the health ministry bar out of the public sum (87 ÷ 153).

The 50% buildings claim is the simple average of 25% and 75%, the 15% equipment claim holds only for Hospital C, and the IT claim holds only for Hospital B's 25%; the simple-average slip that still makes the correct statement true is the one sourceHas names.

3.6 points is the whole fall not averaged, 2.3 points takes the whole fall from 2010 to 2012 (wrong end year and not averaged), and 0.4 points divides by the three years twice; starting from 2009 still lands on 1.2, which sourceHas names.

'B, C, D, A' comes from no slip or pair of slips: ranking by profit alone gives the answer, dividing the wrong way gives A, C, B, D, and swapping one pair of rows gives B, D, C, A or D, B, A, C, but nothing puts D third.

$40 stops at the basic premium, $52 divides the $1.664m evenly over the 32,200 covered policyholders ignoring the 2x ratio, and $109 adds the $29 legal cover to the full premium; leaving the legal cover in gives $211, so no slip lands on $80.

The 57% day-trip claim applies the second pie's share to all riders (wrong base), the 80% 'no purpose except riding' claim over-reads 'main purpose', and the spending claim is the one statement about data not covered that sourceHas lists.

50% is a near-miss estimate of 58 out of 120 (48.3%), the profitability statement is the one statement about data not covered that sourceHas lists, and the Word puzzles claim is a near miss where both games are exactly $0.50m per developer.
